title: What training and professional development must Head Start programs give staff?
description: Head Start training rules under 45 CFR 1302.92: 15 clock hours a year, annual child abuse reporting training, coaching, and the 2026 proposal to rescind them.
shortAnswer: Under 45 CFR 1302.92, a Head Start program must give all new staff, consultants and volunteers an orientation, and run a systematic professional development system in which staff complete at least 15 clock hours of professional development a year, with annual training on mandatory child abuse reporting and on supporting social and emotional development. Education staff must be assessed for a research-based coaching strategy. An August 2026 proposed rule would remove most of these regulatory details.
keyTakeaways: 45 CFR 1302.92(b)(1) sets a floor of 15 clock hours of professional development per year for staff, and section 648A(a)(5) of the Head Start Act separately requires each teacher to attend at least 15 clock hours a year.
Two topics are annual by regulation: mandatory reporting of suspected or known child abuse and neglect, and positive strategies to support children's social and emotional development.
Programs must assess all education staff and offer intensive coaching, including observation, feedback and modeling, to those identified as benefiting most.
The Head Start Act requires an individual professional development plan for every full-time employee who provides direct services to children, regularly evaluated for impact.
As at November 2026, ACF's August 7, 2026 proposed rule would rescind and replace the Performance Standards, keeping only statutory training duties; it is not final.
regulator: Office of Head Start, Administration for Children and Families (ACF), US Department of Health and Human Services
appliesTo: Head Start and Early Head Start grantees and delegate agencies, including Migrant and Seasonal and American Indian and Alaska Native programs
All staff, consultants and volunteers (orientation) and all staff (annual professional development)
Education staff, including teachers, assistant teachers and home visitors (coaching and research-based professional development)
Child and family services staff working on family services, health and disabilities

blocks.text: It requires three things: an orientation for everyone new, a systematic training and professional development system for all staff, and a coordinated coaching strategy for education staff. The rule sits in Subpart I (Human Resources Management) of the [Head Start Program Performance Standards](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-B/chapter-XIII/subchapter-B/part-1302/subpart-I/section-1302.92), last amended by the August 21, 2024 final rule Supporting the Head Start Workforce and Consistent Quality Programming. This page states the rule as at November 2026, from eCFR text current to November 5, 2026.

The orientation under 1302.92(a) must cover, at a minimum, the goals and underlying philosophy of the program and the ways they are implemented. It applies to new staff, consultants and volunteers alike, so a program that relies on community volunteers in classrooms needs an orientation record for each of them, not only for employees.

The professional development system under 1302.92(b) must be designed to help staff gain the knowledge and skills to provide high-quality, comprehensive services within the scope of their jobs, be attached to academic credit as appropriate, and be integrated with the employee engagement practices described in 1302.101(a)(2).

sections.heading: How many hours of professional development do Head Start staff need each year?

blocks.text: At least 15 clock hours per year. Paragraph (b)(1) applies the 15-hour minimum to staff generally, and for teaching staff it adds that the professional development must meet section 648A(a)(5) of the Head Start Act and include individual professional development plans under section 648A(f).

blocks.title: Head Start Act section 648A(a)(5): teacher in-service requirement
blocks.text: "Each Head Start teacher shall attend not less than 15 clock hours of professional development per year. Such professional development shall be high-quality, sustained, intensive, and classroom-focused in order to have a positive and lasting impact on classroom instruction and the teacher's performance in the classroom, and regularly evaluated by the program for effectiveness."

The statutory wording matters for evidence. A log of 15 hours of unrelated webinars may satisfy a simple hour count but not the requirement that teacher professional development be classroom-focused and regularly evaluated for effectiveness. Section 648A(f) of the [Head Start Act](https://headstart.gov/policy/head-start-act/sec-648a-staff-qualifications-development) also requires each agency to create, in consultation with the employee, a professional development plan for all full-time employees who provide direct services to children, and to evaluate those plans regularly for their impact on teacher and staff effectiveness.

sections.heading: Which training topics are required, and which are annual?

blocks.text: Two topics must be delivered every year, and four further areas must be built into the system. The list in 1302.92(b)(2) to (6) is:

items: Annual training on mandatory reporting of suspected or known child abuse and neglect that complies with applicable Federal, State, local and Tribal laws.
Annual training on positive strategies to understand and support children's social and emotional development, such as tools for managing children's behavior.
Training for child and family services staff on best practices for implementing family engagement strategies in a systemic way.

Training for child and family services staff, including staff working on family services, health and disabilities, that builds knowledge, experience and competencies to improve child and family outcomes.

Research-based professional development for education staff focused on effective curricula implementation, the Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework: Ages Birth to Five, partnering with families, supporting children with disabilities, adult-child interactions, dual language learners, challenging behaviors, transitions, and use of data to individualize learning.

blocks.text: Because the child abuse reporting training must follow state and Tribal law, a program operating across state lines needs state-specific content rather than a single national module. The [mandated reporter training page](/regulations/us-school-employee-mandated-reporter-training) explains how state reporting laws differ.

sections.heading: What does the coaching requirement involve?

blocks.text: Programs must implement a research-based, coordinated coaching strategy for education staff under 1302.92(c). It starts with an assessment of all education staff to identify strengths, areas of needed support, and which staff would benefit most from intensive coaching.

items: Staff identified through the assessment must be offered intensive coaching, including opportunities to be observed and to receive feedback and modeling of effective teacher practices tied to program performance goals.
Staff not identified must still have opportunities for other research-based professional development aligned with program performance goals.

Intensive coaching must align with school readiness goals and curricula, use a coach with adequate training and experience in adult learning and in using assessment data, include ongoing communication between the coach, program director and education director, and have clearly articulated goals.
Programs must have policies ensuring assessment results are not used solely to determine punitive actions without giving staff time and resources to improve.

blocks.text: Under 1302.92(d), a program that develops or significantly adapts its approach so that it no longer includes the paragraph (c) elements must partner with external early childhood professional development experts and assess whether the adaptation supports staff adequately.

sections.heading: Is the Head Start training rule changing?

blocks.text: Possibly. On August 7, 2026, ACF published a notice of proposed rulemaking, [Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/08/07/2026-16134/reducing-federal-burden-for-head-start-programs), which proposes to rescind and replace the Performance Standards. Comments closed on October 6, 2026. As at November 2026 no final rule has been published, so 1302.92 remains in force as written.

The proposal states that the Performance Standards would no longer contain specific requirements for staff qualifications and professional development beyond those expressly required by statute, and it would remove the 1302.92(c) coaching requirements. ACF notes in the proposal that programs must continue to meet statutory duties: professional development plans under section 648A(f), at least 15 clock hours of professional development a year for each classroom teacher under section 648A(a)(5), and mentor teacher provisions under section 648A(b).

A separate May 12, 2026 proposed rule, [Restoring Flexibility To Support Head Start Program Access](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/12/2026-09383/restoring-flexibility-to-support-head-start-program-access), targets the wage and benefits provisions of the 2024 workforce rule rather than training. For a method to track changes like these, see [how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change).

sections.heading: What evidence should a Head Start program keep?

blocks.text: Monitoring reviewers look for proof that each requirement happened for each person, so records should be organized by person and by requirement. The table below is an illustrative register; the rows marked statutory would survive the proposed rule even if it is finalized.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each 1302.92 requirement and each Head Start Act duty to learning outcomes and evidence, and tags which ones rest on regulation and which rest on statute. If the proposed rule is finalized, the regulatory items can be retired without losing the statutory ones. See how this works for [public sector and grant-funded organizations](/industries/government-defence).

faqs.q: Do Head Start volunteers need the 15 hours of professional development?
faqs.a: The 15 clock hours in 1302.92(b)(1) apply to staff. Volunteers and consultants must receive the orientation in 1302.92(a), which covers the program's goals, philosophy and how they are implemented. Programs may train volunteers further, but the annual hour floor is written for staff.

faqs.q: Does coaching count toward the 15 clock hours?
faqs.a: The regulation does not exclude it, and the statutory test is that teacher professional development be high-quality, sustained, intensive and classroom-focused, which observation and feedback cycles can meet. Programs should record coaching sessions with dates and durations so they can be counted and evaluated.

faqs.q: Will the 15-hour requirement disappear if the 2026 proposal is finalized?
faqs.a: Not for teachers. The 15 clock hour teacher in-service requirement is in section 648A(a)(5) of the Head Start Act, and ACF's August 2026 proposal says programs must continue to meet it. The regulatory coaching system and the broader staff topic list are what the proposal would remove.

faqs.q: Must the child abuse reporting training be repeated every year?
faqs.a: Yes. 1302.92(b)(2) requires annual training on mandatory reporting of suspected or known child abuse and neglect, and it must comply with applicable Federal, State, local and Tribal laws. Repeating the same national module without state content may not meet that test.

1302.92(b)(2) annual mandatory reporting training; (b)(3) annual social and emotional development training; (b)(4)-(6) family engagement, child and family services, research-based education staff PD topics.

1302.92(c)(1)-(5) coaching strategy: assess all education staff, intensive coaching with observation, feedback and modeling, coach qualifications, non-punitive policy; (d) external experts if adapted.

Head Start Act 648A(a)(5): each teacher not less than 15 clock hours of PD per year, high-quality, sustained, intensive, classroom-focused, regularly evaluated; 648A(f) PD plans for full-time direct service employees.
